login.note: One Stack Exchange account signs in across the network, but sign-in happens per site: the page offers Google/GitHub/Facebook SSO plus email+password, and an SSO path opens a provider window that the human must finish. A new IP or a new profile commonly adds an emailed verification link or a CAPTCHA.

logout.note: The GET only renders a confirmation page; the actual sign-out is a POST carrying the fkey, so a human clicks 'Log out'. It signs the profile out of the whole Stack Exchange network, not just stackoverflow.com.

traps: The session cookies (prov, acct, the per-site auth cookie) are HttpOnly — document.cookie cannot see them, and gating on them reports a live session as logged out.
StackExchange.options.user.fkey EXISTS WHEN SIGNED OUT. It is the request-forgery key, not a session. Gating on fkey is a green light for an anonymous page; gate on userId / isRegistered.

Being signed in to stackoverflow.com does not mean being signed in to superuser.com, serverfault.com or stackexchange.com. The ACCOUNT is network-wide; the SESSION is per site, and each one has its own first sign-in.

Stack Overflow fronts everything with bot protection: a plain non-browser request to stackoverflow.com/questions answers HTTP 403 (observed 2026-09-12 from this machine). Every read has to happen inside the real browser, or through api.stackexchange.com.

Because the probe is written from documentation and never run here, the 'as' it returns may be the display name with reputation glued on — treat the string as a hint until a live verify tidies the selector.
notes: Probe strategy (a) with (b) as a fallback. Primary evidence is the site's own inline config, StackExchange.options.user, which StackExchange.init() writes into every rendered page — userId / isRegistered / isAnonymous is the site's own verdict and needs no network call. The DOM profile link is used only to name the user, never to decide. Fallback (b) is a credentialed same-origin GET of /users/current, which lands on the signed-in user's own profile URL and 404s for anonymous — the final r.url carries both the id and the slug. Cookies are deliberately untouched. UNVERIFIED: written from documentation and the SE userscript conventions, never executed against a live tab; the exact shape of options.user and the topbar selector are the two things a live `verify` should confirm first. A READ recipe should NOT scrape HTML: api.stackexchange.com/2.3 (e.g. /questions?order=desc&sort=activity&site=stackoverflow) serves public reads unauthenticated with no bot wall, and the signed-in-only bits have their own small JSON endpoints on the site itself (/topbar/get-unread-counts returns the inbox/achievement counters for the current session).
